## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The core story is remarkably stable in **structure** and quietly **shifting in substance**. Across all eight quarters Imaz repeats the same three-pillar catechism introduced with the Feb-2024 strategic update: (1) **prioritize shareholder distributions** ("certainty, predictability and upside to our dividend", Q1-24), (2) **defend the balance sheet / credit rating**, and (3) **disciplined net CapEx of €16–19B over the 2024–2027 plan, ~35% low-carbon.** That scaffolding never moves. What moves underneath it is the *source of value* and the *defensive posture*.

**Opening emphasis (Q1–Q3 2024):** an *investment-cycle* story. Repsol is "in the midst of the investment cycle" (Q3-24) — three of the largest organic upstream projects in its history (Alaska/Pikka, Campos 33 Brazil, Leon-Castile Gulf) plus a U.S. renewables build (ConnectGen, Frye solar). The pitch is "invest now, rotate later": grow renewables to 6 GW then sell down. Distribution is funded by a *strong* refining cycle that is visibly rolling over (refining indicator collapses from $11.4/bbl in Q1-24 to **$4/bbl in Q3-24, "71% below a year ago"**).

**Mid-plan pivot (Q4-24 → Q1-25):** the story rotates from *growth-capex* to *capex normalization + portfolio surgery*. Imaz repeatedly flags that "capital expenditures are expected to normalize by 2026 once the investment peak... is complete" and starts guiding net CapEx **down** ("at around or even below €2 billion per year" for upstream, Q3-25). Simultaneously a *new, dominant* growth driver is introduced and steadily amplified: the **"liquidity event"** — an IPO/monetization of the E&P (upstream) vehicle co-owned with EIG. It is first a passing phrase ("preparation for a potential liquidity event", Q4-24) and by Q3-25 has its own capital-markets proof point: a **$2.5B E&P bond, "the largest in U.S. dollars in Repsol's history."**

**Late plan (Q2–Q4 2025):** two structural drivers crystallize and one shock lands.
- **UK consolidation:** the **NEO Energy** merger (Repsol 45% of a 130 kboe/d JV, Q1-25) is upsized in Dec-2025 by folding in **TotalEnergies UK** to create **"Neo Next Plus," ~250 kboe/d in 2026, Repsol 24%.** This is the clearest sum-of-parts value-crystallization move in the set.
- **Customer/retail** is repositioned from a footnote to a hidden crown jewel — Imaz argues retail+power FCF "could pay 60–70%, the 2/3 of the cash dividend of Repsol" (Q3-25), hitting its 2027 EBITDA target (€1.4–1.5B) two years early.
- **Venezuela shock:** the U.S. revokes Repsol's oil license (announced Q2-25, effective 27-May-2025); by Q4-25 (Feb-2026) new U.S. licenses are issued and Imaz makes a striking on-record commitment to **"multiply by 3 in 3 years the production in Venezuela."**

**Quietly dropped / de-emphasized:** the aggressive *renewables growth* drumbeat of 2024 (6 GW, ConnectGen, "demand is eternally growing... AI/data centers") is steadily muted into "rotate assets to crystallize value and **limit our exposure**" (Q4-25) — a textbook narrative contraction from offense (build) to defense (harvest and de-risk). Net: the story has migrated from "we are building the energy-transition major" to "we are a disciplined cash-return machine harvesting a high-graded oil/refining/retail portfolio, with two structural value-unlocks (E&P IPO, UK JV) pending."
